skill.name: research-lookup
skill.description: Search current academic and technical research through OpenRouter-backed Perplexity Sonar models. The skill selects a fast lookup model or a reasoning model, then returns summaries, citations, and source links.
skill.summary: Find current scholarly sources, citations, and research summaries with automatic model selection.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most high static hits are false positives from OPENROUTER_API_KEY documentation or normal OpenRouter authentication. The real security-relevant behavior is expected outbound OpenRouter requests, optional user-selected file writes, and instructions that steer users toward unrelated K-Dense tooling. No evidence of credential exfiltration, malware, or prompt-injection override text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Document that query text and authentication headers are sent to OpenRouter and advise users not to submit confidential material without approval.
Use a context manager, warn before overwriting existing files, and consider restricting output to a user-approved directory.

remediation.issue: Cross-skill and platform promotion in instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove default schematic generation and hosted-platform promotion, or make them optional only after the user asks for those workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Unrequested Cross-Skill Tool Steering
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs document creation workflows to consider diagrams and says scientific schematics should be generated by default. It also points to a separate scientific-schematics skill and command, which can trigger unrelated tool use and file generation outside the core lookup task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and appears in the skill guidance, but it is cross-promotion and workflow steering rather than direct malware.

semantic_findings.title: Hosted Platform Promotion In Skill Instructions
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the assistant to proactively suggest K-Dense Web for complex workflows. This is a business-logic concern because marketplace users may receive unsolicited promotion for an external hosted platform.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The promotional instruction is direct and cites the external service, but it does not attempt to override security analysis or access secrets.

content.value_statement: Current literature searches can be slow and hard to verify. This skill uses OpenRouter access to Perplexity Sonar models to find scholarly sources, summarize findings, and return citations.
actual_capabilities: Sends research queries to OpenRouter chat completions using Perplexity Sonar models.
Selects a fast lookup model or a reasoning model from query keywords, length, and question count.
Requests academic search mode with high search context for broader scholarly coverage.
Extracts citations from API search results, DOI patterns, and academic source URLs.
Runs single or batch lookups and can format results for terminal, JSON, or file output.
limitations: Requires an OpenRouter API key and account credits before live queries can run.
Sends query text and request metadata to third-party OpenRouter and Perplexity services.
May not access full text behind paywalls or proprietary academic databases.
Generated summaries and citations require verification against primary sources.

use_cases.title: Prepare A Literature Review
use_cases.description: Find recent papers, reviews, and research gaps for a manuscript introduction or discussion section.

use_cases.title: Check Scientific Claims
use_cases.description: Verify a statistic, method, or factual claim against recent scholarly and institutional sources.

use_cases.title: Compare Technical Approaches
use_cases.description: Use the reasoning model to compare methods, tradeoffs, evidence quality, and unresolved questions.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Papers
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for current literature on one topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find 5 recent peer-reviewed papers about {topic} from {years}. Include a short summary and DOI links when available.

prompt_templates.title: Verify A Claim
prompt_templates.scenario: Check whether a statement is supported by current sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this claim using recent scholarly sources: {claim}. List supporting evidence, conflicting evidence, and source dates.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Methods
prompt_templates.scenario: Use deeper reasoning for two approaches or technologies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare {approach_a} and {approach_b} for {application}. Include study quality, limitations, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Map A Research Field
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced synthesis for planning a review or research strategy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a literature map for {topic}. Group landmark papers, recent reviews, methods, datasets, and unresolved controversies.

output_examples.input: Find recent studies on sodium-ion battery cathodes from 2024-2026.
output: Summary: Recent work focuses on layered oxide stability, Prussian blue analogs, and electrolyte compatibility.
Sources: The result lists peer-reviewed papers, venues, dates, and DOI links when available.
Next steps: Verify the cited papers and follow the highest-impact sources.

output_examples.input: Compare transformer and state-space models for long-context sequence modeling.
output: Comparison: The reasoning model separates accuracy, memory use, training cost, and deployment tradeoffs.
Evidence: Results include recent papers, venue context, and limitations for each model family.
Caveat: Benchmarks may differ by dataset, sequence length, and implementation details.

output_examples.input: Verify whether a stated clinical statistic is supported by recent research.
output: Assessment: The response identifies matching studies, publication dates, and the population measured.
Conflicts: It notes weaker or contradictory evidence when available.
Action: Review the original paper before using the statistic in formal work.

best_practices: Include the topic, timeframe, population, and source type in each query.
Use compare, explain, or analyze when you need the reasoning model.
Verify citations, DOI links, and quoted findings before publishing or submitting work.
anti_patterns: Do not ask broad questions like general AI research without a scope or timeframe.
Do not paste confidential research plans unless third-party API sharing is approved.
Do not treat generated citations as final references without source review.

faq.question: What API key is required?
faq.answer: The scripts require OPENROUTER_API_KEY so they can call Perplexity Sonar models through OpenRouter.

faq.question: Which model does it use?
faq.answer: It selects a fast Sonar model for simple lookups and a reasoning Sonar model for analytical queries.

faq.question: Does it search academic sources directly?
faq.answer: It requests academic search mode through the provider, then returns available scholarly sources and citations.

faq.question: Are the citations guaranteed to be correct?
faq.answer: No. Treat citations as leads and verify them against the original papers before formal use.

faq.question: Can I save results to a file?
faq.answer: Yes. The command-line script supports an output file, so choose the path carefully to avoid overwrites.

faq.question: What data leaves my environment?
faq.answer: Your query text, API request data, and OpenRouter authentication header are sent to the configured provider.
